articles.title: Red carpet for FPIs': Congress slams Sebi plan to ease disclosure norms for foreign investors
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Congress on Sunday criticised the Securities and Exchange Board of India's (Sebi) proposal to review additional disclosure requirements for
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Congress on Sunday criticised the Securities and Exchange Board of India's (Sebi) proposal to review additional disclosure requirements for foreign portfolio investors (FPIs), saying credibility, transparency and investor protection were essential to efficient financial markets.The opposition party said the proposed changes were a step in the opposite direction and should be "buried", PTI reported.Sebi has proposed removing the additional disclosure framework that requires certain FPIs to provide granular details of entities holding ownership, economic interest or control in them. The regulator said the existing requirements go beyond beneficial ownership identification norms under anti-money laundering rules, making India's disclosure regime more stringent than those in several major global markets.Congress general secretary in-charge communications, Jairam Ramesh, said the consultation paper was issued soon after Prime Minister Narendra Modi addressed industry leaders at FICCI on November 19, proposing to scrap disclosure rules introduced in August 2023 to identify opaque offshore investments in Indian companies."It is clear that the Prime Minister has little hope of reviving domestic private investment, or even FDI, and has decided instead to roll out the red carpet for foreign portfolio investors to keep the stock markets buoyant, even at the cost of market integrity," Ramesh said on X.India needed foreign investors, but not those with opaque and convoluted offshore ownership structures, he said, adding that ease of doing business could not come at the cost of capital market integrity.In August 2023, Sebi required FPIs with more than 50 per cent of their Indian equity investments in a single corporate group to provide detailed disclosures on ultimate ownership, economic interest and control, he said.The disclosures were intended to identify opaque ownership structures that could conceal concentrated control and create opportunities for market abuse, Ramesh added."Now, Sebi proposes to junk these requirements entirely. The loophole that was belatedly closed under pressure after the January 2023 revelations is being reopened," he said.Sebi Chairman Tuhin Kanta Pandey had earlier said the regulator would issue a consultation paper proposing further simplification of FPI regulations, including the removal of certain restrictions that are not present in other countries.Ramesh reiterated that transparency and investor protection were essential to maintaining the credibility of India's financial markets and said the proposed changes should be withdrawn.Money habits form by age 7.
